\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Universal collision bound]
\lean{TCSlib.InformationTheory.IsUniversal}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p067-b005,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p182-b005,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p207-b001
}
\statementsource{HILL99}{pdf-130039751e9f-p020-b009}
\statementsource{CW79}{pdf-1c24478649f7-p002-b005}
\label{TCSlib.InformationTheory.IsUniversal}
\leanok
Let $S$, $\alpha$, and $\beta$ be finite types, and let $f:S\to\alpha\to\beta$. The map
$f$ is universal if, for every pair of distinct elements $x,y\in\alpha$, the number of
$s\in S$ for which $f(s,x)=f(s,y)$ is at most $|S|/|\beta|$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Universality of Affine Hashes]
\lean{TCSlib.InformationTheory.isUniversal_affine}
\statementsource{CW79}{
  pdf-1c24478649f7-p007-b001,
  pdf-1c24478649f7-p007-b003
}
\label{TCSlib.InformationTheory.isUniversal_affine}
\leanok
\uses{TCSlib.InformationTheory.IsUniversal}
\difficulty{4}
Let $F$ be a finite field. The family of maps $x\mapsto ax+b$ from $F$ to $F$, indexed
by $(a,b)\in F\times F$, is universal: for every pair of distinct $x,y\in F$, at most a
fraction $1/|F|$ of the pairs $(a,b)$ satisfy $ax+b=ay+b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Squared sums over fibers]
\lean{TCSlib.InformationTheory.sum_sq_fiber}
\label{TCSlib.InformationTheory.sum_sq_fiber}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets, let $g:A\to B$, and let $w:A\to\mathbb{R}$. Then
\[\sum_{y\in B}\left(\sum_{x\in A:\,g(x)=y}w(x)\right)^2=\sum_{x\in A}\sum_{x'\in A}\begin{cases}w(x)w(x')&g(x)=g(x'),\\0&g(x)\ne g(x').\end{cases}\]
\end{theorem}
